$Comment: MMO Skill Tree's half of the Hallowed set, Hallows_Eve_Hallowed.json. Joins adds this file to that
set instead of making a set of its own, so the player still sees one Hallowed set: one notice,
one entry, one look. The set's name, members and look stay that file's, so this file names none.
Its first tier asks exactly what the set's first tier asks, a piece of the set worn and a Jack
Shield in the utility slot (Armor 1 and Utility 1), so it joins that tier: its stats apply beside the set's,
and its line follows the set's line in the same notice. Its second tier asks the same pieces but
binds its stats with While, and a bound tier never joins another, so it is added as a tier of its
own with a notice line of its own (tier_artillery). A tier asking for something else would be added
the same way. Requires takes this file out on a server without MMO Skill Tree, since these are the
skills' half of the set; always write it with Min 1.
GatherYield and KillYield take whole percent points (5 is +5 on a find's chance): the luck every
gathering find and every kill find rolls with, together the luck every skill's lucky rolls read.
DamageBonus, CommonLib's every-type damage stat, takes whole percent points too (12 is +12%) on
every hit dealt while a bomb or a gun is in hand: the second tier's While is CommonLib's ZigHolding
on the item Families the Artillery skill trains (ItemTag:Family=Bomb, ItemTag:Family=Gun), which
every Lantern Bomb carries through its Parent. It reads the hand, not the hit, so a bomb's burst
counts only while a bomb or a gun is still in hand. It names no MMO Skill Tree condition on purpose:
this pack depends on MMO Skill Tree only optionally, and a condition nobody registered fails the
file's read before Requires can drop it.
All three are Additive on purpose: these channels have a base of zero, so a Multiplicative entry
computes nothing.
